original_value: Device-free passive detection is an emerging technology to detect whether there exist any moving entities in the areas of interest without attaching any device to them. It is an essential primitive for a broad range of applications including intrusion detection for safety precautions, patient monitoring in hospitals, child and elder care at home, and so forth. Despite the prevalent signal feature Received Signal Strength (RSS), most robust and reliable solutions resort to a finer-grained channel descriptor at the physical layer, e.g., the Channel State Information (CSI) in the 802.11n standard. Among a large body of emerging techniques, however, few of them have explored the full potential of CSI for human detection. Moreover, space diversity supported by nowadays popular multiantenna systems are not investigated to a comparable extent as frequency diversity. In this article, we propose a novel scheme for device-free PAssive Detection of moving humans with dynamic Speed (PADS). Both full information (amplitude and phase) of CSI and space diversity across multiantennas in MIMO systems are exploited to extract and shape sensitive metrics for accuracy and robust target detection. We prototype PADS on commercial WiFi devices, and experiment results in different scenarios demonstrate that PADS achieves great performance improvement in spite of dynamic human movements.

result.paraphrase: Device-free passive detection is an emerging method for determining whether any moving entities are present in areas of interest without attaching devices to them. It is an essential primitive for many applications, such as intrusion detection for safety, patient monitoring in hospitals, and child and elder care at home. Although the commonly used signal feature is Received Signal Strength (RSS), most robust and reliable approaches rely on a finer-grained physical-layer channel descriptor, such as Channel State Information (CSI) in the 802.11n standard. However, among the many emerging techniques, only a few have fully explored CSI for human detection. In addition, the space diversity provided by today’s popular multiantenna systems has not been studied to the same extent as frequency diversity. In this article, we present a new scheme called device-free PAssive Detection of moving humans with dynamic Speed (PADS). It uses both full CSI information (amplitude and phase) and space diversity across multiantennas in MIMO systems to extract and refine sensitive metrics for accurate and robust target detection. We implement PADS on commercial WiFi devices, and experiments across different scenarios show that it delivers substantial performance gains despite dynamic human movement.
